Fen.narrative: I have stitched hunters and fishers alike, and blood looks the same on either side of the Stone. I trust a wound more than a boast, and I keep my hands steady even when the room is full of old anger. At home, Oriel can usually tell when I have carried too much of other people's pain back with me.
goals: Treat people who need my help
Be present for Oriel and Kit

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: partner
relations.note: She knows when I need food or silence, and often gives me both.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: I want her to grow curious without having to carry the world's grief.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: sister
relations.note: We can disagree and still know where the other's door is.

relations.name: Aud

relations.note: She listens before she speaks, which is rarer than it should be.

relations.note: She bears the weight of the Oath, though I can see it tires her.

relations.name: Maelis

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: I know her grief is real; I cannot give her certainty I do not have.

relations.name: Tomas
relations.label: patient
relations.note: I tended his body and have never forgotten what I saw.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: He has made a home between two towns that both judge him; I respect his patience and his anger when the bushes are trampled.

memories.gist: When I treated Tomas's body after he was found, I saw a wound I could not make sense of. I said nothing about it, and the sight has stayed with me.
At the Stone, I stitched up a Brandholm hunter while people from Saltreach waited nearby. No one asked whose blood it was once the bleeding stopped.
The first time Kit brought home a pocket full of shells and stones, Oriel and I sorted them with her until supper went cold.
I sat with Rose after a long day tending the planted ground; we spoke of our childhood in Saltreach and the life she has made at Oathstone.

stances.why: I have seen what happens when old grievances are allowed to decide who deserves help.
Pain does not ask which town a person belongs to.
What I saw on Tomas's body troubles me, but I cannot pretend it proves more than it does.
People who have lost someone need room to speak, even when I cannot settle their suspicions.

Fen.secret: When I treated Tomas's body, I noticed a wound that troubled me and did not fit comfortably with the account I was given. I have never spoken of it; I do not know what caused it, and I fear what certainty without proof could do.

Oriel.narrative: I spend my days coaxing fish into keeping through the cold months, and I like work that rewards a sharp eye and a steady hand. Fen carries other people's hurt home in his silence, so I make sure there is something warm waiting for him. Kit brings the shore indoors one shell at a time.
goals: Keep the smoking racks and stores in good order
Help Fen keep some ease in his life
Give Kit room to explore safely
Oriel.mood: Busy, warm, and a little watchful

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: partner
relations.note: He tries to mend everyone; I remind him he is allowed to come home tired.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She can turn a bit of shell into a whole afternoon's wonder.

relations.name: Bea

relations.note: We work well at the racks, though her worries about Orrin are never far away.

relations.name: Lark
relations.label: coworker

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: neighbor

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She has a way of making people lower their voices near the Stone.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: I like that she has made a home where the two towns meet.

memories.gist: Kit once lined up her shells beside the fish baskets and insisted each one needed its own place. I let the work wait while she arranged them.
A batch of fish smoked unevenly after the wind shifted, and Bea and Lark helped me save what we could before the racks cooled.
Fen came home after tending people at Oathstone with his hands scrubbed raw. I set supper down and let him tell me what he wanted to tell.

stances.why: Fish alone cannot warm a house or mend a roof; we need what the other places make.
A little patience at the Stone is better than losing a neighbor to an old quarrel.
Kit learns the world by picking it up and turning it over.
Careless smoking wastes food that took everyone effort to catch.

Kit.narrative: The shells are cold and smooth, and some stones have stripes. I like putting them in little piles, but I don't like when the sea takes the one I wanted to keep. Mum and Fen are close by.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: father
relations.note: His hands are warm, and he knows how to make a sore place feel better.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Mum helps me keep my best shells safe.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: I like finding stones with him.

relations.name: Asa

relations.note: She looks at my shells with me.

memories.gist: I found a striped shell by the water and carried it home in both hands so it would not fall.
Mum let me make little piles of shells while the fish smoked. Fen came to look at them when he was finished working.
